A.summary: PI grants a one-time policy authorization: ordinary source-backed child nodes may receive stable Knowledge-owned canonical identities without per-node PI review when all frozen gates pass; universal roots/families/shared primitives still require PI.
gates: target-specific mapping review supports the concept
semantic boundary is stable enough for identity
no unresolved conflict changes the node's identity
case-only or hypothesis evidence is not sole support
no universal manifestation family/root/shared primitive is introduced

B.summary: Every ordinary stable manifestation node ID returns to PI for approval.
B.tradeoff: Maximum manual control but creates a recurring PI bottleneck and is stricter than the roadmap's ordinary-child-node gate.

G2.title: Normalization evidence threshold for ordinary canonical node identity

A.summary: Allow both source-preserving normalization and transparent/traceable inference to support ordinary canonical node identity, provided normalization epistemic is preserved and target review is supported.

implications.CA01-035: eligible after policy gates; source-preserving process concept
implications.CA01-045: node identity may be eligible, but mapping/runtime remains held by the real-world action prerequisite
implications.CA05-469: career/industry scene concept may be eligible as traceable inferred normalization; person-level event target remains not supported

B.summary: Only source-preserving normalization may create ordinary canonical nodes; inferred normalization remains candidate-only.

implications.CA01-045: node identity potentially eligible but runtime held
implications.CA05-469: held at candidate level despite positive target-specific review

G3.title: Knowledge canonical semantics vs Product compatibility

A.summary: Freeze rich source-native semantics in Knowledge; keep Product fail-closed until a separate adapter/crosswalk work unit can consume them without information loss.
rationale: Product is explicitly an adapter/consumer, not ontology owner
Product v0.1 has no output_kind field
Product event specificity is coarser than the PI-accepted Knowledge values
CA01-045's real-world action prerequisite is not representable by current router antecedents

B.summary: Force Knowledge canonical semantics into the current Product node vocabulary.
B.risk: Loses or conflates the output_kind and fine-grained event-specificity distinctions accepted under D1-D5.

C.summary: Change Product schema/runtime directly from the Core work unit.
C.risk: Violates lane ownership and mixes ontology governance with consumer implementation.

after_recommended_approval.next_core_action: Define and validate a Knowledge-owned canonical manifestation node artifact/ID policy, then canonicalize only ordinary child nodes meeting the approved gates; mapping promotion remains separately gated.
after_recommended_approval.product_action: No immediate Product modification. Prepare a later Product-owned adapter/crosswalk work unit after a Knowledge canonical artifact exists.
